_comment: For every number shown on the website, this file records where it comes from. Paper = the latest public PDF (https://www.emmawiles.com/storage/reskill.pdf). Repo files are relative to the repository root.

sources.paper_pdf_repo_draft: writeup/reskill (9).pdf (OLDER DRAFT — titled 'Generative AI as a Temporary Exoskeleton for Upskilling Knowledge Workers'; superseded by the latest public PDF)

claims.source: Paper Introduction ('a randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving 986 consultants') and Methods; Table 1 first row
claims.note: Table 1 header prints 983 while the two arms (493+493) sum to 986; text uses 986. Flagged for author review.

claims.claim: 573 began the survey; used as N in the latest abstract
487 participants in the analysis sample (submitted both tasks)
claims.source: Paper Methods / Results ('For the 487 participants who submitted output')

claims.claim: 44 data scientists set the benchmark (normalized to 0)

claims.repo: computed_objects/experimental_data.csv, columns CodingProcessGradeRelativeNorm, StatsOverallRelativeNorm, PSMAEGradeAdjusted, treatment_arm; reproduced by scripts/verify_from_source.py
claims.transformation: Group means (already DS-normalized) for treatment_arm 0/1; treatment effect and 95% CI from OLS with HC0 robust SEs. Prediction score = -1 x PSMAEGradeAdjusted.

claims.claim: Figure 2: effects by prior coding experience; competent coders 5pp below benchmark on coding and statistics; Bayes factors 0.25 (coding) and 0.37 (statistics)
claims.repo: computed_objects/experimental_data.csv, column know_code; reproduced by scripts/verify_from_source.py
claims.transformation: Means and OLS treatment effects within each know_code level; classical 95% CIs matching the paper's Figure 2. Bayes factors quoted from paper text.

claims.claim: Figure 3: no evidence of improved unaided knowledge; TEs -7.7 to +4.8pp; F(5,198)=0.83, p=0.531; Bayes factors 0.10/0.18/0.50/0.13/0.62
claims.source: Paper Figure 3, Section 2.3, and Appendix Table B14
claims.repo: writeup/tables/learning.tex; data/complete_data_all.dta, columns DSKnowledgeQ1Correct..Q5Correct; reproduced by scripts/verify_from_source.py
claims.transformation: Full-sample control/treatment shares and OLS treatment effects with HC0 robust SEs. These match the plotted bars and the paper text.
claims.note: The latest PDF's Figure 3 note lists per-question Ns (323/270/270/151/270) from a task-started subsample, but the plotted bars and text statistics correspond to the full sample (573/399/418/253/408). Flagged for author review.

claims.claim: Figure 4: treated workers more confident GPT-4 could solve problems it cannot; significant for all four 'cannot do' questions
claims.source: Paper Figure 4, Section 2.4, and Appendix Table B8
claims.transformation: Treatment-effect coefficients (percentage points of confidence 0-100) and control base rates quoted directly from Table B8; 95% CIs computed as estimate +/- 1.96 x SE.
